author: Marcus R. Brown
description:
Pins the JSDoc parsing behavior the documentation pipeline depends on, and brings `docs/` into the test graph for the first time.

## Why

`docs/scripts/extract-jsdoc.ts` parses every JSDoc comment that becomes API documentation, using `doctrine` — archived since 2018-12-03 (#2032).

Nothing is broken. The concern is how this pipeline fails. Two defects found recently produced silently wrong documentation while CI stayed green (#2017, #2022), and `docs/typedoc.json` sets `skipErrorChecking: true`, which turns resolution failures into bad output rather than errors (#2023).

`extract-jsdoc.ts:201` has the same shape:

```ts
} catch {
  // Continue looking for other comments
}
```

A parse failure is indistinguishable from "no JSDoc here."

## What it tests

Doctrine's `parse(text, {unwrap: true})` directly, with the exact options the pipeline uses, against fixtures taken from real components. The pipeline reads only two fields, so those are what get pinned:

```ts
description = jsdoc.description || ''
examples = jsdoc.tags?.filter(tag => tag.title === 'example')...
```

Seven tests: plain description, `@example` with an intact `tsx` code fence, multiple examples in source order, `@param`/`@returns`/`@remarks` not polluting the description, non-standard hyphenated tags, `@default`, and the short single-line prop comment form.

Fixtures 1-6 come from `Button.tsx` and `Form.tsx` verbatim or lightly condensed, cited in comments. Fixture 7 is synthetic — no verbatim single-line prop comments exist in the codebase today.

Assertions pin **observed** behavior, not ideal behavior. The point is detecting change.

## A finding, not a failure

Writing the test surfaced real silent corruption. Doctrine splits hyphenated tag names at the first hyphen:

@theme-tokens uses color.primary
